3 pitches, 4th/low-5th class
rope up for the 3-pitch 5.4 ridge climb

contradictions.why: The header/stats field pitches says 4, but pitch_detail lists exactly 3 pitches and the itinerary note, itinerary schedule, and two waypoint notes all independently say 3 pitches.

claims.says: Downclimb/scramble the ridge back toward the North-South notch (3rd/4th class with a few exposed steps); many parties place one short rappel off blocks near the top of the red slab rather than downclimbing it.
most parties do the descent in three rappels with a single 60m rope

contradictions.why: descent frames the normal descent as downclimbing with at most one optional short rappel; descent_text frames it as a full three-rappel descent from the summit. These describe materially different amounts of rope work.
contradictions.internal_resolution: descent_text is corroborated by rappel_detail (3 numbered stations) and rappel_count_note; descent_text is also the longer field so it is what actually renders per the page's own rule, but the two fields still disagree internally.

contradictions.fact: rappel sequence/count on the shared South Ridge descent

claims.says: then make a double-rope rappel to a large platform, a single-rope rappel to a lower slab, and a final double-rope rappel to the base

three rappels on two 60 m ropes (four rappels if you carry a single 60 m rope), going first via a single-strand rappel off a two-bolt anchor to a narrow ledge, then a full-rope-length rappel... and a final rappel to the base ledges

contradictions.why: descent implies 4 rappels in a double/single/double pattern; descent_text says 3 rappels in a single/double/(final) pattern, matching the South Ridge route's own documented rappel_detail order (single, double, single).
contradictions.internal_resolution: descent_text matches the shared South Ridge route's own rappel_detail sequence; descent's 4-rappel double/single/double account is the outlier.

contradictions.internal_resolution: descent_text is corroborated by rappel_detail (3 stations, including a mandatory double-rope final rappel) and rappel_count_note; descent's downclimb framing is the outlier, though descent_text (longer) is what actually renders.

N/NW
the peak's north/west-facing slopes
broad north-facing slabs and talus on the peak's east/left side

up the broad south-facing slabs and talus on the peak's east/left side
Ascend granite slabs and blocks on the peak's south side/slopes to the summit

contradictions.why: Route name, aspect, face, and the main approach prose all say the standard line climbs north/northwest-facing slopes, while climbing_route, the final pitch_detail row, and a waypoint literally named 'Base of south slopes' describe the identical final approach to the summit as south-facing. A climber comparing Overview (face) to the Plan tab's WAYPOINTS/ROUTE BREAKDOWN would get opposite compass directions for the same terrain.
contradictions.internal_resolution: Cannot be resolved from the row alone — roughly half the fields support each direction. Notably the route's own id, wa_little_annapurna_south_slopes, matches the 'south' fields while the displayed name 'North Slopes' matches the 'north' fields, suggesting two versions were merged.

Snow Lakes Trailhead
Icicle Creek Road

contradictions.why: approach_logistics, the waypoints array, road, the main approach prose, and itinerary all agree the route is reached via the Snow Lakes Trailhead / Icicle Creek Road. But beta instead routes the climber via Colchuck Lake and Aasgard Pass (a different range-crossing entirely), and face/pitch_detail describe an Ingalls Creek/Crystal Creek approach with a '~7.5 mile' hike and a '6,000 ft basin below Crystal Lake' — this exact wording and figures match the unrelated Little Annapurna South Face route's approach, indicating contaminated/copied text.
contradictions.internal_resolution: Snow Lakes Trailhead is correct — confirmed by approach_logistics.trailhead, waypoints, road, and the itinerary schedule ('Leave Snow Creek trailhead'); beta, face, and pitch_detail are the contaminated outliers.

contradictions.why: gain_ft is about 27% below both the itinerary's own gainFt and the route's own loss_ft for what is an out-and-back day, where gain and loss should be roughly equal.
contradictions.internal_resolution: loss_ft and itinerary.gainFt agree with each other at 8100; gain_ft (6364) is the outlier (also flagged by the mechanical detector).

contradictions.fact: total gain/loss/distance vs the itinerary's own day-by-day sums

claims.says: roughly 8,100+ ft of cumulative gain/loss (the profile crosses Longs Pass twice) over about 12 mi round trip

contradictions.why: The header stats (gain_ft/loss_ft 8100, dist_km 19.3 ≈ 12 mi) are corroborated by the route's own itinerary.totalNote prose, but the itinerary's own per-day gainFt/lossFt/miles fields sum to only 5,175 ft / 15.9 mi — a climber reading the day-by-day plan would budget for meaningfully less elevation gain and more distance than the route's own summary states.
contradictions.internal_resolution: gain_ft/loss_ft/dist_km match totalNote's own prose (8,100+ ft, ~12 mi) and reflect the profile crossing Longs Pass twice; the itinerary's day-level numbers are the outlier and appear to omit part of the return trip.

claims.says: Enchantment permit area: overnight stays May 15-Oct 31 require a quota permit (Recreation.gov advance lottery); day trips need the free self-issued day-use permit at the trailhead.
Free Self-Issue Day Permit
approached on Alpine Lakes Wilderness ground under the Cle Elum Ranger District — free self-issued trailhead permit, Northwest Forest Pass to park, no Enchantment lottery permit

contradictions.why: The route's top-level permit field is generic Enchantment-lottery boilerplate, but the route approaches via Esmeralda/Goat Pass (Alpine Lakes Wilderness, Cle Elum Ranger District), and its own Goat Pass bivy entry explicitly says 'no Enchantment lottery permit' for that exact ground; access.permit similarly only names a free self-issue day permit.
contradictions.internal_resolution: access.permit and the Goat Pass bivy note agree (no lottery); the top-level permit field's Enchantment-lottery claim is the outlier, likely copied from an Enchantments-zone route.

claims.says: Esmeralda Basin Trailhead (FR-9737)
Stuart Lake Trailhead (Eightmile Creek Rd #7601)
This pin is the Icicle-side start, not the Teanaway one.

contradictions.why: The TRAILHEAD card (approach_logistics.trailhead) names Esmeralda Basin Trailhead, but the route's waypoints array itself starts at Stuart Lake Trailhead on the opposite (Icicle Creek) side of the range. The waypoint's own note acknowledges two different approach variants exist, but the two rendered fields still name different trailheads as 'the' starting point.
contradictions.internal_resolution: Both are legitimate documented approach_variants (one marked primary: the Ingalls Lake/Goat Pass line matching approach_logistics), so this is a data-selection inconsistency between which variant each field defaults to, rather than one being flatly wrong.
